finding.text: There is no `requirements.md` in this task folder, so I reviewed against the brief its `task.jsonl` points to: `voice-20261015/ask-00dc4855.md`. The second ask in that brief was "fix the system so future voice masterminds can spawn masterminds without a special grant", and this change does that.

`Servex/agents/policy.js:149`: the new line lets any `mastermind-*` or `task-mastermind-*` id spawn the role `mastermind`, and it runs before the worker check. This is exactly the hard check the brief names, and the smallest fix there is: one line. `policy.test.mjs` passes on the branch (61 checks).

`policy.js:169`: the new `rules()` row says "spawn mastermind, minion and helper" for `task-mastermind-X` too. A task mastermind actually spawns like a manager (anything outside `NO_SPAWN`), plus a mastermind now. The row is accurate for `mastermind-X` only, so it should read "mastermind-X: spawn mastermind, minion and helper; task-mastermind-X: also mastermind".

The grant covers only the role `mastermind`. A voice mastermind still cannot spawn `task-mastermind`, `page-mastermind` or `manager`. That fits the owner's words ("page mastermind, AI mastermind" are spawned with the mastermind role), but if anyone uses the `page-mastermind` role word, it is still refused.

The fix takes effect only after Servex restarts. The brief deliberately does not restart it, because the voice tunnel runs through Servex, so the open item "retry the page and AI masterminds" still has to wait for that restart.
The architecture doc section (`Servex/agents/doc/architecture.md`) records the owner's reasoning as a quote with a link to the brief, as the owner asked. Words are plain and the section is short.

There is still no `requirements.md` in this folder, so this pass reviews against the brief `task.jsonl` names, [ask-00dc4855.md](../ask-00dc4855.md). Its second ask is "fix the system so future voice masterminds can spawn masterminds through the tunnel MCP without a special grant", and `Servex/agents/policy.js:149` does exactly that, in one line, at the hard check the brief named.

Traced by hand: `mastermind-voice-1` is kind `worker`, so the new line lets it spawn a `mastermind`, and the worker line still lets it spawn minions and helpers; `task-mastermind-x` keeps its manager-like spawning and adds `mastermind`; assistants, the master assistant and external tabs are still refused, because their checks run first. I could not re-run `policy.test.mjs` from a scratch copy (it needs `express`, and the junction guard rightly blocks linking the main `node_modules`); round 1 recorded 61 passing checks.
The round-1 finding about `rules()` is fixed (`policy.js:167` and `:169`): `task-mastermind-*` now reads "spawn like a manager, and also a mastermind", and `mastermind-X` has its own row.

`Servex/agents/doc/architecture.md:127` says any mastermind may spawn "a `mastermind`, a minion or a helper". That is true of `mastermind-*` only, because a `task-mastermind-*` may spawn more (like a manager). Saying "may also spawn a `mastermind`" would match the code.

The grant goes by name: `is_mastermind()` (`policy.js:48`) is a prefix test on the id. If a worker can choose a child's name, a child named `mastermind-…` gains the right to spawn masterminds. This is low risk, since the owner says the role "adds little power", but it is worth checking that `Agents.name()` mints the `mastermind-` prefix only for the `mastermind` role.
The fix only takes effect after Servex restarts, which the brief deliberately puts off. The open item "retry the page and AI masterminds" waits on that restart, so it should stay visible on the card.
Simpler way: none. One guard line, one test line and one doc section is the minimum. The owner's reasoning is recorded as a quote that links to the brief, as asked.
